Long-time grazing PML in a dispersive medium Evolve a finite packet with an 80-degree central phase angle to T = 700, isolating boundary error against a no-PML reference on the same grid. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use c = 1 and a homogeneous Lorentz medium with epsilon_inf = 1, delta_epsilon = 0.2 and omega_0 = 12 continuing through the PML. Joint refinement uses 512/768/1024 cells and peaks 6/9/12. The normal coarse control has peak 6; the damped fine companion has peak 12. Length 64, layer thickness 12, center 32, width 4 and carrier 6 are fixed. Editorial clarification The central angle is 80 degrees; finite kx bandwidth gives neighboring angles. The no-PML reference shares the discretization and initialization to isolate boundary error from bulk dispersion. Small operator and finite-trajectory checks do not prove global stability for arbitrary angles and materials. The joint family does not measure fixed-PML spatial order; the older 100 checks alone do not prove peak-12 global stability. One transverse y period is shown. The displayed x and y scales differ to make the fields visible. Adopted numerical method Couple Yee and midpoint ADE updates to a trapezoidal derivative-memory filter at native times.
